Team — FYI from Anya (procurement asks). Quick thoughts below, looking for guidance on flex credits vs invoicing cadence before I respond:

1) Invoice cadence: Borealis prefers two invoices in year 1 (split prepay). We can accommodate if they accept a nominal finance fee (0.5% of prepay) or if we shift 10% of credits to a year-1-smoothing credit.

2) Pull-forward / reallocation: I suggested a reallocation policy: unused phase credits can be moved to later phases if they notify 30 days ahead, but cannot be refunded. Alternatively, offer a small refundable buffer (up to 15% of phase commitment) with a 90-day notice.

3) SLA protection: propose an SLA credit ladder: 5% credit if p95 latency misses target month 1–3, escalating to 10% if persistent over 2 consecutive months.

Questions:
- Monica, will finance sign off on split invoice with the proposed finance fee?
- Markus, do we have precedent for a refundable buffer on phased commitments?

I'll draft a clean reply for Anya once we align.

Thanks,

Priya — finance ok with a two-invoice split for year 1 if the total prepay is recognized up front for revenue-deferral purposes (we need signed SOW before revenue recognition). The 0.5% finance fee is acceptable but I prefer we absorb the fee for strategic deals; instead we should ask for a slightly larger nonrefundable commitment on phase 1 (12% vs 10%).

On refunds: we generally do not do cash refunds on unused capacity. A refundable buffer as an exception is possible but must be limited: max 10% of phase value, refunded pro rata at year-end and only with 90-day notice. Otherwise credits roll forward for up to 12 months.

SLA credits: we can support the ladder, but any SLA credit must be capped at 25% of the monthly invoice and cannot reduce below a minimum gross margin threshold. Legal will add a carve-out for force majeure and planned maintenance windows.

Monica
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

- Phase sizes: Borealis wants phase 1 to be 20 GPUs (not 10) to cover an initial pilot. Can we compress the cost curve so year-1 effective price per GPU is within 8% of the 3-year blended rate?
- Refundable buffer: procurement prefers 15% refundable buffer on phase 1 (we're asking due to uncertainty on the pilot). If you can’t do 15% refundable, we would accept 10% refundable but want the refund to be available after month 6 rather than year-end.
- SLA escalation: acceptable. We will not push for credits beyond 30% monthly cap.

We can sign a marked-up SOW by next Wednesday if we settle these three bullets.

Regards,

Anya / Tim / Procurement — attaching the updated term schedule and a redline SOW (SOW-Borealis-draft.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Schedule_v3.xlsx). Summary of changes since last thread: 

1) Phase sizing: we agree to 20 GPUs for Phase 1. To keep the blended economics intact we reprofiled discounts so year-1 effective GPU price is ~6.5% above the 3-year blended rate (better than the 8% target you asked for).

2) Refundable buffer: we will allow a refundable buffer of up to 10% of Phase 1 prepaid value. Refunds become available after month 6 and are processed pro rata at the next quarterly invoice. Rationale: balances Borealis flexibility and Redwood financial controls.

3) Invoice cadence: we accept two invoices in year 1 (50/50 split). Redwood will recognize revenue in accordance with ASC/IFRS rules once the signed SOW is returned. There is no finance fee — Redwood will absorb it for this strategic engagement.

4) SLA credits: we agree the ladder described earlier, capped at 30% monthly and with the standard carve-outs for maintenance/force majeure. Legal will provide a short SOW exhibit with the metrics and credit calculations.

Next steps: if this summary aligns, please sign the attached SOW and we’ll convert the draft to a final PO-ready agreement. Jordan, can you confirm the billing contact and PO terms once they sign? Monica, please confirm revenue recognition checklist is queued. Markus, flag if any executive approval is needed for the refundable buffer exception.

Thanks — look forward to getting this across the line.
